description: Every night for fifteen years, Mary saw the same picture in her sleep: a dark room, a camera flash, a pale beckoning hand… and a dog grinning with very human teeth.

In 1992, a link to a picture called smile.jpg appeared on a small Chicago bulletin board. About 400 people saw it. Only Mary ever talked about it. Years later, a young writer goes looking for her story, and the picture starts looking for him.
A Scroll Kaos paper-cutout horror story. Watch until the very end.

top: - **Story rights (important):** the Creepypasta.com page names no author ("By Creepypasta.com", April 28, 2010). Other sites also call the author unknown; one site says Michael Lutz wrote it (UNVERIFIED). The legend may be older than that page (UNVERIFIED). **Before you monetise, contact Creepypasta.com and ask about narration rights.** Whether permission is needed, and who can give it, is UNVERIFIED.
- The famous image is not used: our dog is an original drawing (no polaroid look, no blood, no fingerprints, no copy or trace of the famous photo).
flags.age_restriction: - Age-restriction risk: a creepy grin with human teeth; a death is mentioned but never shown; no injuries and no blood. YouTube may still age-restrict it (UNVERIFIED).
bottom: - Non-graphic changes: in the original, Mary takes her own life; here the narration only says "Mary had died… It said nothing about how." Shock-site names were removed and real site names were made general. Seizures are only mentioned as claims inside the legend.
- Photosensitive safety: no flashing or strobe anywhere; the camera flash is drawn as a still pool of light.
- Reel shortening: the Reel keeps every main beat and the ending, but shortens the internet-legend part, the fakes, the hallway wait and the narrator's fears at the end.
